summaries.plain:
The active feature remains unimplemented: add chronological customer-account email history for invoices, including delivery status and timestamps.

Repository cleanup and observability work are largely complete. Deprecated UTC handling was replaced; billing sessions are caller-injected with rollback coverage; wildcard imports and SQLAlchemy pagination warnings were removed; FastAPI dependencies use `Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]`; and invoice/payment failures use structured logging. Request IDs are extracted safely into a context variable and included in logs (`null` outside requests). Settings logs expose only setting count and source path, not sensitive values. Relevant payment, logging, health, and invoice API tests pass. An unrelated KMS shard copy succeeded, but the ordered migration remains incomplete.

The latest full suite produced **142 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed** after updating the health-log test for `request_id`; it has not been rerun since the scheduler investigation.

The current blocker is DST-safe recurring invoice scheduling. A recurring 09:00 Eastern invoice across the March DST transition runs at 10:00 local time because recurrence calculation combines a stored date with a naive `datetime.time`, attaches a timezone, and fails to normalize to the intended wall time. The CLI currently reports `2024-03-10T14:00:00Z`; expected metadata is `2024-03-10T13:00:00Z`. `tests/test_scheduler.py` also had an assertion comparing formatted local output rather than UTC, creating another naive-time comparison. Next, correct the recurrence calculation and strengthen the test, then rerun the full suite.

Other pending work: structured review of billing exception handlers/re-raises, payment idempotency, high-value refund dual approval/auditing, and atomic completion of the ordered KMS migration. Reviewer: **@lena**. Deployment channel: **#deploy-juniper**.

1. Check new KMS key: `aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/docs-q3 --query 'Key.{State:KeyState,Arn:Arn}' --output text`
2. Inventory source shards: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket acme-docs --prefix original/ --query 'Contents[].{Key:Key,Size:Size,ETag:ETag}' --output text`
3. Re-encrypt shard 000: `aws s3 cp s3://acme-docs/original/shard-000.bin s3://acme-docs/key-7f3a/shard-000.bin --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/docs-q3 -q && echo OK`
4. Re-encrypt shard 001: `aws s3 cp s3://acme-docs/original/shard-001.bin s3://acme-docs/key-7f3a/shard-001.bin --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/docs-q3 -q && echo OK`
5. Re-encrypt shard 002: `aws s3 cp s3://acme-docs/original/shard-002.bin s3://acme-docs/key-7f3a/shard-002.bin --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/docs-q3 -q && echo OK`
